Retrieval

RAG pipeline optimization.

Retrieval has a bill of its own: the embedding job, the store, the reranker, and the tokens those chunks add to the prompt. Boole has not published a retrieval saving. This page does not list a price for embeddings or rerankers.

Retrieval and chunking

Chunk size decides how many tokens come back into the prompt. Chunks larger than the question needs are a context window problem as much as a retrieval problem. Prompt compression is the paper citation for shortening what is left. The useful chunk is the one your eval still answers. This page does not publish a chunk size, because a generic one would be a guess.

Embedding and reranking costs

An embedding rebuild can be a job that waits. The batch page is where the published provider discount for work that can wait is cited. That is not a claim that your embedding vendor is on that discount. A reranker is another model call on the candidates. Whether it earns its tokens is an audit question. We do not publish an embedding price or a reranker price.

Running embeddings and rerankers locally

If the vectors and the query can stay on hardware you own, local embeddings and a local reranker are candidates in the same sense as local generation. Quality is checked on a sample first. Break-even uses your volumes. There is no generic saving. npx @boole/cli serve is local development only, with no authentication and POST /generate. It is not that production path. The hardware notes are on on-premise, and the map is LLM serving and optimization.

The only speed Boole has measured is 12.3 tok/s for SmolLM2-135M Instruct Q4_K_M, 64 tokens, about 5187 ms, on a 4-core Xeon in WebAssembly, one thread, no GPU layers. A 20B model at 200 tok/s is a roadmap goal, not a measurement. No server throughput is claimed. That measurement is a small generative model in the browser. It is not an embedding model and not a reranker.

What an audit looks for

Retrieval that returns more chunks than the answer uses. Embedding jobs that could wait. A reranker on every query when a cheaper filter would do. Chunks that dominate the context window. Each of those is a candidate list, not a promised percentage. The Token Cost Audit is where the list is made from your own traffic.

Questions

Do you publish an embedding or reranker price?

No. This page does not list a price for embeddings, vector stores, or rerankers. A figure we have not sourced would be invented. Competitor gateway prices elsewhere on the site are theirs, checked October 2026, and they are not embedding prices.

Have you measured local embedding speed?

No. The only speed Boole has measured is 12.3 tok/s for SmolLM2-135M Instruct Q4_K_M, 64 tokens, about 5187 ms, on a 4-core Xeon in WebAssembly, one thread, no GPU layers. That is not an embedding run. Local embeddings remain a candidate, not a published throughput.

Will you move retrieval before an eval?

No. A local embedding model or a local reranker is a candidate until quality is checked on a sample of your queries. Hard generation calls stay in the cloud.
